claims.statement: OpenWiki telemetry is opt-out and emits exactly one PostHog event, TELEMETRY_RUN_EVENT ("openwiki_run"), per completed init or update run, carrying command/outcome/environment and (on failure) error classification.
isTelemetryDisabled returns true when OPENWIKI_TELEMETRY_DISABLED or DO_NOT_TRACK is set to a truthy value, and recordRun short-circuits (sending nothing) when it is disabled.

CI runs are still sent but are tagged ci:true and attributed to a per-provider sentinel id (ci-<provider>) rather than a unique install id, so ephemeral runners never inflate the human install count; only explicit opt-out stops sending.

Every event is stamped with production provenance derived from build origin (isProductionBuild, true only when running from dist/, not from NODE_ENV) and a build_channel that is "official" only for npm-published upstream builds, so real usage and official-release signal can be separated from dev/fork telemetry.

Identity is an anonymous per-machine random-UUID install id stored at ~/.openwiki/install-id with owner-only permissions (file 0o600, home dir 0o700), created lazily; the id has no relationship to the user, machine, or repository.

firstRunNoticePending returns true only on the run that mints the install id (isNew), returns false and mints no id when opted out or in CI (noticeSuppressed), and never throws; the CLI calls it once at startup before any event is sent and renders single-sourced disclosure copy from config.ts.

withRunTelemetry is the single boundary that records an openwiki_run event, wrapping the whole setup->connectors->agent sequence so a throw anywhere in it is recorded exactly once, and it rethrows the original error after recording so the CLI still owns the failure UX.

withRunTelemetry threads a mutable RunTelemetryContext through the run: the agent publishes the resolved provider onto it the instant resolution succeeds and publishes a noop outcome for an update short-circuit; a clean return defaults to success and a throw records failure with describeErrorForTelemetry diagnostics.

recordRunSafe is the run-lifecycle-to-telemetry bridge: it drops chat (so only init/update emit events), maps output mode to the brain mode, and attaches setup fields (mode, provider, configuredConnectors) on init only, omitting them on updates; like recordRun it never throws.

buildRunEvent is a pure builder (no IO, no process state) that is the single source of truth for the openwiki_run payload, spreading in setup and failure fields only when present, so successful and update payloads omit them; this keeps the production sender and the seed script from drifting apart.
Configured connector ids are flattened into boolean connector_<id> properties (present = configured) rather than an array, making connector adoption a dimension without array unnesting.

The event is sent via PostHog captureImmediate (whose promise is the single HTTP request) awaited under a 3s FLUSH_TIMEOUT_MS bound, deliberately not the queued capture()+shutdown flush path that can drop events, and the timeout guarantees telemetry never stalls the short-lived CLI.
capture returns false (sends nothing) when no PostHog key is configured.

The --telemetry-file tee writes the exact record to an unguessable owner-only (0o600) scratch sibling opened with flag "wx" (refusing to follow a pre-planted symlink) and atomically renames it into place, defeating symlink attacks and permission leakage in shared directories; a failed tee logs to stderr but never fails the run.

Every event sets $process_person_profile:false so PostHog never builds a person (unique-install counts still work off the install-id distinctId) and sends disableGeoip:true so no server-side geoip enrichment occurs, with the raw client IP additionally discarded server-side.
Raw error strings, messages, and provider strings never enter the telemetry payload; the failure path emits only closed-set enum members and bare integers.
TelemetryErrorClass is a closed set of failure families with agent_error as the residual bucket for anything matching no rule (the quality meter that should trend toward zero).

inStage/inStageSync bracket a pipeline stage (config->build->run->finalize) and stamp thrown errors with an ErrorOriginTag carried on a non-enumerable symbol so it never serializes into a payload or JSON dump; the tag records stage and, for owned families, the class/detail decided at the throw site, with first tag winning.

Classification walks a nearest-first, cycle-safe, depth-bounded (MAX_UNWRAP_DEPTH=32) unwrap chain so a provider error hidden inside a wrapper or AggregateError is recovered rather than collapsing into the residual: classifyError returns the first named class, readErrorOrigin returns the first owned-family tag, and firstStatusInChain surfaces the nearest HTTP status.

A build_error/stream_open origin tag is overridden by the raw classification when the failure carries a provider signal (a provider_error classification, or an HTTP status paired with any named class), so a disguised provider failure at the first round trip is attributed to the provider rather than counted as an OpenWiki build bug, while a signal-less stream-setup failure keeps its tag.

errorDetail is the anonymity spine: normalizeErrorDetail validates each observed detail against a hardcoded per-family allowlist (FIXED_ERROR_DETAILS) and drops off-list values to undefined; connector_error/tool_error carry a registry id validated at the tag site instead.

For the residual agent_error bucket the detail is the innermost error's own name (innermostErrorName from the cause chain), gated by isSafeErrorIdentifier (a bare identifier of at most 64 chars) so a name carrying a path, URL, space, or user value is rejected and the anonymity envelope stays closed.

deriveOwner is the single source of owner truth mapping (class, detail, stage) to environment/provider/openwiki/unowned/control, encoding cross-owner exceptions PostHog cannot derive: provider_error auth/quota_exceeded and network_error dns/refused route to environment, and filesystem_error at finalize routes to openwiki.

Telemetry behavior is verified under test/telemetry with posthog-node and ci-info mocked for determinism, covering event shape/gating, the run wrapper, the run-fact bridge, the no-key send path, and the install-id lifecycle.
